I've been using Chromebooks for a few years now. My last one (which was my first) was a little Samsung Chromebook, and I'd setup a crouton install on it for a while. Since it was ARM based, however, there were too many things I couldn't run to make the Linux install worth a crap.

My current Chromebook is an Acer CB5-571, and running a crouton install in it was pretty slick, but I'd still run into weirdness here and there since it wasn't a normal install.

The other day I stumbled upon GalliumOS, which is a distro built specifically for Chromebooks (so the wifi, trackpad, menu keys, etc. all work), and took the plunge to do a custom BIOS so I could wipe the ChromeOS and boot directly to Gallium.

Folks, it's a whole different laptop anymore. Not only was the install quick and painless, the OS itself is a well done Xubuntu variant that's fast and stable. Considering you can pick these things up for under $300, it's definitely worth checking out.
